sentences.en: Philosophers, dramatists, theologians have grappled with this question for centuries: what makes people go wrong?
Interestingly, I asked this question when I was a little kid.
I grew up in the South Bronx, inner-city ghetto in New York, and I was surrounded by evil, as all kids are who grew up in an inner city.
And I had friends who were really good kids, who lived out the Dr. Jekyll Mr. Hyde scenario -- Robert Louis Stevenson.
That is, they took drugs, got in trouble, went to jail.
Some got killed, and some did it without drug assistance.
So when I read Robert Louis Stevenson, that wasn't fiction.
The only question is, what was in the juice?

And more importantly, that line between good and evil -- which privileged people like to think is fixed and impermeable, with them on the good side, the others on the bad side -- I knew that line was movable, and it was permeable.
Good people could be seduced across that line, and under good and some rare circumstances, bad kids could recover with help, with reform, with rehabilitation.
So I want to begin with this wonderful illusion by [Dutch] artist M.C. Escher.
If you look at it and focus on the white, what you see is a world full of angels.
But let's look more deeply, and as we do, what appears is the demons, the devils in the world.
That tells us several things. One, the world is, was, will always be filled with good and evil, because good and evil is the yin and yang of the human condition.
It tells me something else. If you remember, God's favorite angel was Lucifer.
Apparently, Lucifer means "the light." It also means "the morning star," in some scripture.
And apparently, he disobeyed God, and that's the ultimate disobedience to authority.
And when he did, Michael, the archangel, was sent to kick him out of heaven along with the other fallen angels.
And so Lucifer descends into hell, becomes Satan, becomes the devil, and the force of evil in the universe begins.
Paradoxically, it was God who created hell as a place to store evil.
He didn't do a good job of keeping it there though.

So, this arc of the cosmic transformation of God's favorite angel into the Devil, for me, sets the context for understanding human beings who are transformed from good, ordinary people into perpetrators of evil.
So the Lucifer effect, although it focuses on the negatives -- the negatives that people can become, not the negatives that people are -- leads me to a psychological definition.
Evil is the exercise of power. And that's the key: it's about power.
To intentionally harm people psychologically, to hurt people physically, to destroy people mortally, or ideas, and to commit crimes against humanity.
If you Google "evil," a word that should surely have withered by now, you come up with 136 million hits in a third of a second.
sentences.zh: 如果你用谷歌搜索“邪恶”这个词，这个词现在肯定已经消失了，你会在三分之一秒内得到 1.36 亿次点击。

sentences.en: A few years ago -- I am sure all of you were shocked, as I was, with the revelation of American soldiers abusing prisoners in a strange place in a controversial war, Abu Ghraib in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我相信你们所有人都像我一样，对美国士兵在一场有争议的战争中在一个陌生的地方虐待囚犯的消息感到震惊，那就是伊拉克的阿布格莱布监狱。

sentences.en: And these were men and women who were putting prisoners through unbelievable humiliation.
sentences.zh: 这些男男女女让囚犯遭受难以置信的羞辱。

sentences.en: I was shocked, but I wasn't surprised, because I had seen those same visual parallels when I was the prison superintendent of the Stanford Prison Study.
sentences.zh: 我很震惊，但并不感到惊讶，因为当我担任斯坦福监狱研究的监狱长时，我也看到了同样的视觉相似之处。

sentences.en: Immediately the Bush administration military said what?
sentences.zh: 布什政府军方立即说什么？

sentences.en: What all administrations say when there's a scandal: "Don't blame us. It's not the system.
sentences.zh: 当出现丑闻时，所有政府都会说：“不要责怪我们。这不是系统的问题。

sentences.en: It's the few bad apples, the few rogue soldiers."
sentences.zh: 这是少数坏苹果，少数流氓士兵。”

sentences.en: My hypothesis is, American soldiers are good, usually.
sentences.zh: 我的假设是，美国士兵通常都很优秀。

sentences.en: Maybe it was the barrel that was bad. But how am I going to deal with that hypothesis?
sentences.zh: 也许是桶坏了。但我该如何应对这个假设呢？

sentences.en: I became an expert witness for one of the guards, Sergeant Chip Frederick, and in that position, I had access to the dozen investigative reports.
sentences.zh: 我成为其中一名警卫奇普·弗雷德里克中士的专家证人，在那个职位上，我可以获得十几份调查报告。

sentences.en: I had access to him. I could study him, have him come to my home, get to know him, do psychological analysis to see, was he a good apple or bad apple.
sentences.zh: 我可以接触到他。我可以研究他，让他来我家，了解他，做心理分析，看看他是好人还是坏人。

sentences.en: And thirdly, I had access to all of the 1,000 pictures that these soldiers took.
sentences.zh: 第三，我可以访问这些士兵拍摄的所有 1,000 张照片。

sentences.en: These pictures are of a violent or sexual nature.
sentences.zh: 这些图片具有暴力或色情性质。

sentences.en: All of them come from the cameras of American soldiers.
sentences.zh: 全部都来自美国大兵的相机。

sentences.en: Because everybody has a digital camera or cell phone camera, they took pictures of everything, more than 1,000.
sentences.zh: 因为大家都有数码相机或者手机摄像头，什么都拍，一千多张。

sentences.en: And what I've done is I organized them into various categories.
sentences.zh: 我所做的就是将它们分为不同的类别。

sentences.en: But these are by United States military police, army reservists.
sentences.zh: 但这些都是由美国宪兵、陆军预备役人员执行的。

sentences.en: They are not soldiers prepared for this mission at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不是为执行此任务而准备的士兵。

sentences.en: And it all happened in a single place, Tier 1-A, on the night shift.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在一个地方，即 1-A 层的夜班。

sentences.en: Why? Tier 1-A was the center for military intelligence.
sentences.zh: 为什么？ 1-A 层是军事情报中心。

sentences.en: It was the interrogation hold. The CIA was there.
sentences.zh: 这是审讯拘留。中央情报局在那里。

sentences.en: Interrogators from Titan Corporation, all there, and they're getting no information about the insurgency.
sentences.zh: 泰坦公司的审讯人员都在那里，但他们没有得到任何有关叛乱的信息。

sentences.en: So they're going to put pressure on these soldiers, military police, to cross the line, give them permission to break the will of the enemy, to prepare them for interrogation, to soften them up, to take the gloves off.
sentences.zh: 所以他们要向这些士兵、宪兵施加压力，让他们越过界限，允许他们打破敌人的意志，让他们做好审讯的准备，让他们软化，让他们脱下手套。

sentences.en: Those are the euphemisms, and this is how it was interpreted.
sentences.zh: 这些都是委婉说法，这就是它的解释方式。

sentences.en: Let's go down to that dungeon. (Typewriting) [Abu Ghraib Iraq Prison Abuses 2008 Military Police Guards' Photos] [The following images include nudity and graphic depictions of violence]
sentences.zh: 我们去那个地牢吧。 （打字）【2008年阿布格莱布伊拉克监狱虐待事件宪兵警卫照片】【以下图片包含裸体和暴力画面描述】

sentences.en: (Camera shutter sounds) (Thuds)
sentences.zh: （相机快门声）（轰鸣声）

sentences.en: (Camera shutter) (Camera shutter)
sentences.zh: （相机快门） （相机快门）

sentences.en: (Breathing) (Bells) (Bells end)
sentences.zh: （呼吸）（铃声）（铃声结束）

sentences.en: So, pretty horrific. That's one of the visual illustrations of evil.
sentences.zh: 所以，非常可怕。这是邪恶的视觉例证之一。

sentences.en: And it should not have escaped you that the reason I paired the prisoner with his arms out with Leonardo da Vinci's ode to humanity is that prisoner was mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 你不应该忽视的是，我之所以将张开双臂的囚犯与列奥纳多·达·芬奇的人性颂歌配对，是因为该囚犯患有精神疾病。

sentences.en: That prisoner covered himself with shit every day, they had to roll him in dirt so he wouldn't stink.
sentences.zh: 那个犯人每天浑身上下都是屎，还得用泥土把他滚起来，不让他发臭。

sentences.en: But the guards ended up calling him "Shit Boy."
sentences.zh: 但警卫最终称他为“狗屎男孩”。

sentences.en: What was he doing in that prison rather than in some mental institution?
sentences.zh: 他在那座监狱而不是在某个精神病院里做什么？

sentences.en: In any event, here's former Secretary of Defense Rumsfeld.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这是前国防部长拉姆斯菲尔德。

sentences.en: He comes down and says, "I want to know, who is responsible?
sentences.zh: 他下来说道：“我想知道，谁该负责？

sentences.en: Who are the bad apples?" Well, that's a bad question.
sentences.zh: 谁是坏苹果？”嗯，这是一个糟糕的问题。

sentences.en: You have to reframe it and ask, "What is responsible?"
sentences.zh: 你必须重新构建它并问：“什么负责？”

sentences.en: "What" could be the who of people, but it could also be the what of the situation, and obviously that's wrongheaded.
sentences.zh: “什么”可以指人的身份，也可以指情况的情况，显然这是错误的。

sentences.en: How do psychologists try to understand such transformations of human character, if you believe that they were good soldiers before they went down to that dungeon?
sentences.zh: 如果你相信心理学家在进入地牢之前是好士兵，那么他们如何试图理解人类性格的这种转变？

sentences.en: There are three ways. The main way is called dispositional.
sentences.zh: 有三种方法。主要的方式称为处置。

sentences.en: We look at what's inside of the person, the bad apples.
sentences.zh: 我们看的是一个人的内心，即坏苹果。

sentences.en: This is the foundation of all of social science, the foundation of religion, the foundation of war.
sentences.zh: 这是所有社会科学的基础、宗教的基础、战争的基础。

sentences.en: Social psychologists like me come along and say, "Yeah, people are the actors on the stage, but you'll have to be aware of the situation.
sentences.zh: 像我这样的社会心理学家会说：“是的，人们是舞台上的演员，但你必须意识到这种情况。

sentences.en: Who are the cast of characters? What's the costume?
sentences.zh: 角色阵容有哪些？服装是什么？

sentences.en: Is there a stage director?" And so we're interested in what are the external factors around the individual -- the bad barrel?
sentences.zh: 有舞台导演吗？”所以我们感兴趣的是个人周围的外部因素是什么——坏桶？

sentences.en: Social scientists stop there and they miss the big point that I discovered when I became an expert witness for Abu Ghraib.
sentences.zh: 社会科学家就此止步，他们忽略了我在成为阿布格莱布监狱专家证人时发现的要点。

sentences.en: The power is in the system. The system creates the situation that corrupts the individuals, and the system is the legal, political, economic, cultural background.
sentences.zh: 权力在系统里。制度创造了腐蚀个体的情境，制度就是法律、政治、经济、文化背景。

sentences.en: And this is where the power is of the bad-barrel makers.
sentences.zh: 这就是坏桶制造商的力量所在。

sentences.en: If you want to change a person, change the situation.
sentences.zh: 如果你想改变一个人，就先改变情况。

sentences.en: And to change it, you've got to know where the power is, in the system.
sentences.zh: 要改变它，你必须知道系统中的权力在哪里。

sentences.en: So the Lucifer effect involves understanding human character transformations with these three factors.
sentences.zh: 因此，路西法效应涉及通过这三个因素来理解人类性格的转变。

sentences.en: And it's a dynamic interplay. What do the people bring into the situation?
sentences.zh: 这是一种动态的相互作用。人们给这种情况带来了什么？

sentences.en: What does the situation bring out of them?
sentences.zh: 这种情况给他们带来了什么？

sentences.en: And what is the system that creates and maintains that situation?
sentences.zh: 创造并维持这种情况的系统是什么？

sentences.en: My recent book, "The Lucifer Effect," is about, how do you understand how good people turn evil?
sentences.zh: 我最近的书《路西法效应》是关于，你如何理解好人如何变成邪恶的？

sentences.en: And it has a lot of detail about what I'm going to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 其中有很多关于我今天要讨论的内容的细节。

sentences.en: So Dr. Z's "Lucifer Effect," although it focuses on evil, really is a celebration of the human mind's infinite capacity to make any of us kind or cruel, caring or indifferent, creative or destructive,
sentences.zh: 因此，Z博士的“路西法效应”虽然关注的是邪恶，但实际上是对人类思想无限能力的庆祝，它使我们任何人变得善良或残忍，关心或冷漠，富有创造力或破坏性，

sentences.en: and it makes some of us villains. And the good news that I'm going to hopefully come to at the end is that it makes some of us heroes.
sentences.zh: 这让我们中的一些人变成了恶棍。我希望最后能得到的好消息是，它使我们中的一些人成为英雄。

sentences.en: This wonderful cartoon in the New Yorker summarizes my whole talk: "I'm neither a good cop nor a bad cop, Jerome.
sentences.zh: 《纽约客》上的这幅精彩漫画总结了我的整个演讲：“杰罗姆，我既不是好警察，也不是坏警察。

sentences.en: Like yourself, I'm a complex amalgam of positive and negative personality traits that emerge or not, depending on the circumstances."
sentences.zh: 和你一样，我是一个积极和消极人格特质的复杂混合物，这些特质的出现与否取决于具体情况。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) There's a study some of you think you know about, but very few people have ever read the story.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 你们中有些人认为自己知道一项研究，但很少有人读过这个故事。

sentences.en: You watched the movie. This is Stanley Milgram, little Jewish kid from the Bronx, and he asked the question, "Could the Holocaust happen here, now?"
sentences.zh: 你看过这部电影。这是斯坦利·米尔格拉姆，来自布朗克斯的犹太小孩子，他问了一个问题：“大屠杀现在会发生在这里吗？”

sentences.en: People say, "No, that's Nazi Germany, Hitler, you know, that's 1939."
sentences.zh: 人们说：“不，那是纳粹德国，希特勒，你知道，那是 1939 年。”

sentences.en: He said, "Yeah, but suppose Hitler asked you, 'Would you electrocute a stranger?' 'No way, I'm a good person.'"
sentences.zh: 他说：“是的，但是假设希特勒问你，‘你会电死一个陌生人吗？’ “没办法，我是个好人。”

sentences.en: He said, "Why don't we put you in a situation and give you a chance to see what you would do?"
sentences.zh: 他说：“我们为什么不把你置于一个情境中，给你一个机会，看看你会做什么？”

sentences.en: And so what he did was he tested 1,000 ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 所以他所做的就是对 1000 名普通人进行了测试。

sentences.en: 500 New Haven, Connecticut, 500 Bridgeport.
sentences.zh: 500 纽黑文，康涅狄格州，500 布里奇波特。

sentences.en: And the ad said, "Psychologists want to understand memory.
sentences.zh: 广告中写道：“心理学家想要了解记忆。

sentences.en: We want to improve people's memory, because it is the key to success."
sentences.zh: 我们希望提高人们的记忆力，因为这是成功的关键。”

sentences.en: OK? "We're going to give you five bucks -- four dollars for your time.
sentences.zh: 好的？ “我们将给你五美元——四美元作为你的时间。

sentences.en: We don't want college students. We want men between 20 and 50."
sentences.zh: 我们不想要大学生。我们想要20岁到50岁之间的男性。”

sentences.en: In the later studies, they ran women. Ordinary people: barbers, clerks, white-collar people.
sentences.zh: 在后来的研究中，他们跑的是女性。普通人：理发师、店员、白领。

sentences.en: So, you go down, one of you will be a learner, one will be a teacher.
sentences.zh: 所以，你们下去，你们中的一个将成为学习者，一个将成为老师。

sentences.en: The learner's a genial, middle-aged guy.
sentences.zh: 学习者是一位和蔼可亲的中年男子。

sentences.en: He gets tied up to the shock apparatus in another room.
sentences.zh: 他被绑在另一个房间的电击装置上。

sentences.en: The learner could be middle-aged, could be as young as 20.
sentences.zh: 学习者可能是中年人，也可能只有20岁。

sentences.en: And one of you is told by the authority, the guy in the lab coat, "Your job as teacher is to give him material to learn.
sentences.zh: 权威人士、穿着实验服的家伙告诉你们中的一个人，“作为老师，你的工作就是给他提供学习材料。

sentences.en: Gets it right, reward. Gets it wrong, you press a button on the shock box.
sentences.zh: 做对了，奖励。弄错了，你按一下震动盒上的按钮。

sentences.en: The first button is 15 volts. He doesn't even feel it."
sentences.zh: 第一个按钮是 15 伏。他甚至没有感觉到。”

sentences.en: That's the key. All evil starts with 15 volts.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键。一切邪恶都是从 15 伏开始的。

sentences.en: And then the next step is another 15 volts.
sentences.zh: 然后下一步是另外 15 伏。

sentences.en: The problem is, at the end of the line, it's 450 volts.
sentences.zh: 问题是，线路末端的电压为 450 伏。

sentences.en: And as you go along, the guy is screaming, "I've got a heart condition! I'm out of here!"
sentences.zh: 当你继续前行时，那家伙尖叫着，“我有心脏病！我要离开这里！”

sentences.en: You're a good person. You complain. "Sir, who will be responsible if something happens to him?"
sentences.zh: 你是个好人。你抱怨。 “先生，如果他出了什么事，谁来负责？”

sentences.en: The experimenter says, "Don't worry, I will be responsible.
sentences.zh: 实验者说：“放心，我会负责的。

sentences.en: Continue, teacher." And the question is, who would go all the way to 450 volts?
sentences.zh: 继续吧，老师。”问题是，谁会一直使用 450 伏电压？

sentences.en: You should notice here, when it gets up to 375, it says, "Danger. Severe Shock."
sentences.zh: 您应该注意到这里，当它达到 375 时，它会显示“危险。严重休克”。

sentences.en: When it gets up to here, there's "XXX" -- the pornography of power.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，就是“XXX”——权力的色情。

sentences.en: So Milgram asks 40 psychiatrists, "What percent of American citizens would go to the end?"
sentences.zh: 因此米尔格拉姆问 40 名精神科医生，“有百分之多少的美国公民愿意走到最后？”

sentences.en: They said only one percent. Because that's sadistic behavior, and we know, psychiatry knows, only one percent of Americans are sadistic.
sentences.zh: 他们说只有百分之一。因为这是施虐行为，而且我们知道，精神病学也知道，只有百分之一的美国人有施虐倾向。

sentences.en: OK. Here's the data. They could not be more wrong.
sentences.zh: 好的。这是数据。他们大错特错了。

sentences.en: Two thirds go all the way to 450 volts. This was just one study.
sentences.zh: 三分之二的电压一直达到 450 伏。这只是一项研究。

sentences.en: Milgram did more than 16 studies. And look at this.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆做了超过 16 项研究。看看这个。

sentences.en: In study 16, where you see somebody like you go all the way, 90 percent go all the way.
sentences.zh: 在研究 16 中，你看到像你这样的人一路走来，90% 的人一路走来。

sentences.en: In study five, if you see people rebel, 90 percent rebel.
sentences.zh: 在研究五中，如果你看到人们叛逆，90% 的人都会叛逆。

sentences.en: What about women? Study 13 -- no different than men.
sentences.zh: 那么女性呢？研究 13——与男性没有什么不同。

sentences.en: So Milgram is quantifying evil as the willingness of people to blindly obey authority, to go all the way to 450 volts.
sentences.zh: 因此，米尔格拉姆将邪恶量化为人们盲目服从权威、一路承受 450 伏电压的意愿。

sentences.en: And it's like a dial on human nature. A dial in a sense that you can make almost everybody totally obedient, down to the majority, down to none.
sentences.zh: 这就像人性的表盘。从某种意义上说，你可以让几乎每个人都完全服从，低至大多数，低至没有。

sentences.en: What are the external parallels? For all research is artificial.
sentences.zh: 外部的相似之处是什么？因为所有的研究都是人为的。

sentences.en: What's the validity in the real world? 912 American citizens committed suicide or were murdered by family and friends in Guyana jungle in 1978, because they were blindly obedient to this guy, their pastor -- not their priest -- their pastor, Reverend Jim Jones.
sentences.zh: 在现实世界中的有效性是什么？ 1978年，912名美国公民在圭亚那丛林自杀或被家人和朋友谋杀，因为他们盲目服从这个人，他们的牧师——而不是他们的神父——他们的牧师吉姆·琼斯牧师。

sentences.en: He persuaded them to commit mass suicide.
sentences.zh: 他说服他们集体自杀。

sentences.en: And so, he's the modern Lucifer effect, a man of God who becomes the Angel of Death.
sentences.zh: 所以，他就是现代的路西法效应，一个成为死亡天使的神人。

sentences.en: Milgram's study is all about individual authority to control people.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆的研究都是关于控制他人的个人权力。

sentences.en: Most of the time, we are in institutions, so the Stanford Prison Study is a study of the power of institutions to influence individual behavior.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，我们都在机构中，因此斯坦福监狱研究是对机构影响个人行为的力量的研究。

sentences.en: Interestingly, Stanley Milgram and I were in the same high school class in James Monroe in the Bronx, 1954.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，1954 年，斯坦利·米尔格拉姆和我在布朗克斯区詹姆斯·门罗的高中同班。

sentences.en: I did this study with my graduate students, especially Craig Haney -- and it also began work with an ad.
sentences.zh: 我和我的研究生，特别是克雷格哈尼一起做了这项研究，它也开始与广告一起工作。

sentences.en: We had a cheap, little ad, but we wanted college students for a study of prison life.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个廉价的小广告，但我们想要大学生来研究监狱生活。

sentences.en: 75 people volunteered, took personality tests.
sentences.zh: 75 人自愿参加了性格测试。

sentences.en: We did interviews. Picked two dozen: the most normal, the most healthy.
sentences.zh: 我们做了采访。选了两打：最正常的，最健康的。

sentences.en: Randomly assigned them to be prisoner and guard.
sentences.zh: 随机分配他们为囚犯和看守。

sentences.en: So on day one, we knew we had good apples.
sentences.zh: 所以从第一天起，我们就知道我们买到了好苹果。

sentences.en: I'm going to put them in a bad situation.
sentences.zh: 我会让他们处于一个糟糕的境地。

sentences.en: And secondly, we know there's no difference between the boys who will be guards and those who will be prisoners.
sentences.zh: 其次，我们知道将成为警卫的男孩和将成为囚犯的男孩之间没有区别。

sentences.en: To the prisoners, we said, "Wait at home. The study will begin Sunday."
sentences.zh: 我们对囚犯说：“在家等一下。学习将于周日开始。”

sentences.en: We didn't tell them that the city police were going to come and do realistic arrests.
sentences.zh: 我们没有告诉他们市警察会来进行实际的逮捕。

sentences.en: (Video) (Music) [Day 1] Student: A police car pulls up in front, and a cop comes to the front door,
sentences.zh: （视频）（音乐）【第一天】学生：一辆警车停在前面，一名警察来到前门，

sentences.en: and knocks, and says he's looking for me.
sentences.zh: 然后敲门，说他在找我。

sentences.en: So they, right there, you know, they took me out the door, they put my hands against the car.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就在那里，你知道，他们把我带出了门，他们把我的手放在车上。

sentences.en: It was a real cop car, it was a real policeman, and there were real neighbors in the street, who didn't know that this was an experiment.
sentences.zh: 这是一辆真正的警车，这是一位真正的警察，街上还有真正的邻居，他们不知道这是一个实验。

sentences.en: And there was cameras all around and neighbors all around.
sentences.zh: 周围都是摄像头，周围都是邻居。

sentences.en: They put me in the car, then they drove me around Palo Alto.
sentences.zh: 他们把我放进车里，然后开车带我绕帕洛阿尔托转了一圈。

sentences.en: They took me to the basement of the police station.
sentences.zh: 他们把我带到派出所的地下室。

sentences.en: Then they put me in a cell. I was the first one to be picked up, so they put me in a cell, which was just like a room with a door with bars on it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把我关进牢房。我是第一个被抓起来的，所以他们把我关进一个牢房，就像一个房间，门上有铁栅栏。

sentences.en: You could tell it wasn't a real jail. They locked me in there, in this degrading little outfit.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出这不是真正的监狱。他们把我锁在那里，穿着这件有辱人格的小衣服。

sentences.en: They were taking this experiment too seriously.
sentences.zh: 他们太认真地对待这个实验了。

sentences.en: Here are the prisoners, who are going to be dehumanized, they'll become numbers.
sentences.zh: 这些囚犯将被非人化，他们将成为数字。

sentences.en: Here are the guards with the symbols of power and anonymity.
sentences.zh: 这里是带有权力和匿名象征的守卫。

sentences.en: Guards get prisoners to clean the toilet bowls out with their bare hands, to do other humiliating tasks.
sentences.zh: 狱警让囚犯徒手清理马桶，或者做其他羞辱性的工作。

sentences.en: They strip them naked. They sexually taunt them.
sentences.zh: 他们剥光他们的衣服。他们对他们进行性嘲弄。

sentences.en: They begin to do degrading activities, like having them simulate sodomy.
sentences.zh: 他们开始进行有辱人格的活动，比如让他们模拟鸡奸。

sentences.en: You saw simulating fellatio in soldiers in Abu Ghraib.
sentences.zh: 你在阿布格莱布监狱见过士兵模拟口交。

sentences.en: My guards did it in five days. The stress reaction was so extreme that normal kids we picked because they were healthy had breakdowns within 36 hours.
sentences.zh: 我的警卫在五天内就完成了。压力反应如此极端，以至于我们挑选的健康孩子在 36 小时内就崩溃了。

sentences.en: The study ended after six days, because it was out of control.
sentences.zh: 该研究在六天后结束，因为它失去了控制。

sentences.en: Five kids had emotional breakdowns. Does it make a difference if warriors go to battle changing their appearance or not?
sentences.zh: 五个孩子情绪崩溃。战士们上战场时改变外貌有什么区别吗？

sentences.en: If they're anonymous, how do they treat their victims?
sentences.zh: 如果他们是匿名的，他们会如何对待受害者？

sentences.en: In some cultures, they go to war without changing their appearance.
sentences.zh: 在某些文化中，他们在打仗时不会改变自己的外表。

sentences.en: In others, they paint themselves like "Lord of the Flies."
sentences.zh: 在其他人中，他们把自己描绘成“蝇王”。

sentences.en: In some, they wear masks. In many, soldiers are anonymous in uniform.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，他们戴着口罩。在许多地方，穿着制服的士兵都是匿名的。

sentences.en: So this anthropologist, John Watson, found 23 cultures that had two bits of data.
sentences.zh: 因此，这位人类学家约翰·沃森 (John Watson) 发现了 23 种拥有两位数据的文化。

sentences.en: Do they change their appearance? 15. Do they kill, torture, mutilate? 13.
sentences.zh: 他们会改变外貌吗？ 15. 他们会杀人、折磨、残害吗？ 13.

sentences.en: If they don't change their appearance, only one of eight kills, tortures or mutilates.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不改变外貌，八次杀戮、酷刑或残害中只有一次。

sentences.en: The key is in the red zone. If they change their appearance, 12 of 13 -- that's 90 percent -- kill, torture, mutilate.
sentences.zh: 钥匙在红色区域。如果他们改变外貌，13 人中的 12 人——即 90%——就会杀人、折磨、残害。

sentences.en: And that's the power of anonymity. So what are the seven social processes that grease the slippery slope of evil?
sentences.zh: 这就是匿名的力量。那么，导致罪恶滑坡的七个社会过程是什么呢？

sentences.en: Mindlessly taking the first small step. Dehumanization of others. De-individuation of self.
sentences.zh: 无意识地迈出第一步。他人的非人化。自我去个体化。

sentences.en: Diffusion of personal responsibility. Blind obedience to authority.
sentences.zh: 个人责任的分散。盲目服从权威。

sentences.en: Uncritical conformity to group norms. Passive tolerance of evil through inaction, or indifference.
sentences.zh: 不加批判地遵守群体规范。通过不作为或冷漠来被动容忍邪恶。

sentences.en: And it happens when you're in a new or unfamiliar situation.
sentences.zh: 当你处于新的或不熟悉的情况时，这种情况就会发生。

sentences.en: Your habitual response patterns don't work.
sentences.zh: 你的习惯反应模式不起作用。

sentences.en: Your personality and morality are disengaged.
sentences.zh: 你的人格和道德脱节了。

sentences.en: "Nothing is easier than to denounce the evildoer; nothing more difficult than understanding him," Dostoyevsky.
sentences.zh: 陀思妥耶夫斯基说：“没有什么比谴责恶人更容易的了；没有什么比理解他更困难的了。”

sentences.en: Understanding is not excusing. Psychology is not excuse-ology.
sentences.zh: 理解不是借口。心理学不是借口学。

sentences.en: So social and psychological research reveals how ordinary, good people can be transformed without the drugs.
sentences.zh: 因此，社会和心理学研究揭示了如何在不使用药物的情况下改变普通的好人。

sentences.en: You don't need it. You just need the social-psychological processes.
sentences.zh: 你不需要它。你只需要社会心理过程。

sentences.en: Real world parallels? Compare this with this.
sentences.zh: 现实世界的相似之处？这个跟这个比较一下。

sentences.en: James Schlesinger -- I'm going to end with this -- says, "Psychologists have attempted to understand how and why individuals and groups who usually act humanely can sometimes act otherwise in certain circumstances."
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·施莱辛格（James Schlesinger）——我将以此作为结束——说，“心理学家试图理解通常表现人道的个人和团体如何以及为什么有时在某些情况下会表现出不同的行为。”

sentences.en: That's the Lucifer effect. And he goes on to say, "The landmark Stanford study provides a cautionary tale for all military operations."
sentences.zh: 这就是路西法效应。他接着说：“斯坦福大学这项具有里程碑意义的研究为所有军事行动提供了警示。”

sentences.en: If you give people power without oversight, it's a prescription for abuse.
sentences.zh: 如果你在没有监督的情况下赋予人们权力，那就是滥用权力的处方。

sentences.en: They knew that, and let that happen. So another report, an investigative report by General Fay, says the system is guilty.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这一点，并让这种情况发生。因此，另一份报告，即费伊将军的调查报告，称该系统有罪。

sentences.en: In this report, he says it was the environment that created Abu Ghraib, by leadership failures that contributed to the occurrence of such abuse, and because it remained undiscovered by higher authorities for a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 他在这份报告中表示，正是环境造就了阿布格莱布监狱，领导失误导致了此类虐待事件的发生，而且很长一段时间没有被上级当局发现。

sentences.en: Those abuses went on for three months. Who was watching the store?
sentences.zh: 这些虐待行为持续了三个月。谁在看店？

sentences.en: The answer is nobody, I think on purpose.
sentences.zh: 答案是没有人，我是故意的。

sentences.en: He gave the guards permission to do those things, and they knew nobody was ever going to come down to that dungeon.
sentences.zh: 他允许守卫做这些事情，他们知道没有人会来到那个地牢。

sentences.en: So you need a paradigm shift in all of these areas.
sentences.zh: 因此，您需要在所有这些领域进行范式转变。

sentences.en: The shift is away from the medical model that focuses only on the individual.
sentences.zh: 这种转变远离了只关注个人的医疗模式。

sentences.en: The shift is toward a public health model that recognizes situational and systemic vectors of disease.
sentences.zh: 这种转变是朝着认识疾病的情境性和系统性媒介的公共卫生模式转变。

sentences.en: Bullying is a disease. Prejudice is a disease.
sentences.zh: 欺凌是一种病。偏见是一种病。

sentences.en: Violence is a disease. Since the Inquisition, we've been dealing with problems at the individual level.
sentences.zh: 暴力是一种疾病。自宗教裁判所以来，我们一直在个人层面上处理问题。

sentences.en: It doesn't work. Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn says, "The line between good and evil cuts through the heart of every human being."
sentences.zh: 这不起作用。亚历山大·索尔仁尼琴说：“善与恶之间的界限贯穿每个人的心。”

sentences.en: That means that line is not out there. That's a decision that you have to make, a personal thing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这条线不存在。这是你必须做出的决定，是个人的事情。

sentences.en: So I want to end very quickly on a positive note.
sentences.zh: 所以我想尽快以积极的态度结束。

sentences.en: Heroism as the antidote to evil, by promoting the heroic imagination, especially in our kids, in our educational system.
sentences.zh: 英雄主义是邪恶的解药，通过在我们的教育系统中促进英雄想象力，特别是在我们的孩子身上。

sentences.en: We want kids to think, "I'm a hero in waiting, waiting for the right situation to come along, and I will act heroically.
sentences.zh: 我们希望孩子们这样想：“我是一个等待中的英雄，等待合适的情况出现，我会采取英雄行动。

sentences.en: My whole life, I'm now going to focus away from evil -- that I've been in since I was a kid -- to understanding heroes.
sentences.zh: 我的一生，现在将把注意力从我从小就参与的邪恶中转移出来，去理解英雄。

sentences.en: Banality of heroism. It's ordinary people who do heroic deeds.
sentences.zh: 英雄主义的平庸。做出英雄事迹的都是普通人。

sentences.en: It's the counterpoint to Hannah Arendt's "Banality of Evil."
sentences.zh: 这是汉娜·阿伦特的《平庸之恶》的对立面。

sentences.en: Our traditional societal heroes are wrong, because they are the exceptions.
sentences.zh: 我们传统的社会英雄是错误的，因为他们是例外。

sentences.en: They organize their life around this. That's why we know their names.
sentences.zh: 他们围绕这个组织自己的生活。这就是为什么我们知道他们的名字。

sentences.en: Our kids' heroes are also wrong models for them, because they have supernatural talents.
sentences.zh: 我们孩子们的英雄对他们来说也是错误的榜样，因为他们拥有超自然的天赋。

sentences.en: We want our kids to realize most heroes are everyday people, and the heroic act is unusual.
sentences.zh: 我们希望我们的孩子意识到大多数英雄都是普通人，而英雄行为是不寻常的。

sentences.en: This is Joe Darby. He was the one that stopped those abuses you saw, because when he saw those images, he turned them over to a senior investigating officer.
sentences.zh: 这是乔·达比。他是那个制止了你所看到的那些虐待行为的人，因为当他看到这些图像时，他将它们交给了一名高级调查官员。

sentences.en: He was a low-level private, and that stopped it.
sentences.zh: 他是一名低级二等兵，这就阻止了这一切。

sentences.en: Was he a hero? No. They had to put him in hiding, because people wanted to kill him, and then his mother and his wife.
sentences.zh: 他是英雄吗？不。他们不得不把他藏起来，因为人们想杀死他，然后是他的母亲和妻子。

sentences.en: For three years, they were in hiding. This is the woman who stopped the Stanford Prison Study.
sentences.zh: 他们躲藏了三年。这是停止斯坦福监狱研究的女人。

sentences.en: When I said it got out of control, I was the prison superintendent.
sentences.zh: 当我说事情失控时，我是监狱长。

sentences.en: I didn't know it was out of control. I was totally indifferent.
sentences.zh: 我不知道事情已经失控了。我完全无动于衷。

sentences.en: She saw that madhouse and said, "You know what, it's terrible what you're doing to those boys.
sentences.zh: 她看到了那个疯人院，说道：“你知道吗，你对那些男孩做的事情太可怕了。

sentences.en: They're not prisoners nor guards, they're boys, and you are responsible."
sentences.zh: 他们不是囚犯，也不是看守，他们是男孩，你要对此负责。”

sentences.en: And I ended the study the next day. The good news is I married her the next year.
sentences.zh: 第二天我就结束了研究。好消息是我第二年就娶了她。

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) I just came to my senses, obviously.
sentences.zh: （笑声）（掌声）显然，我刚刚醒悟过来。

sentences.en: So situations have the power to do [three things].
sentences.zh: 因此，情境有能力做[三件事]。

sentences.en: But the point is, this is the same situation that can inflame the hostile imagination in some of us, that makes us perpetrators of evil, can inspire the heroic imagination in others.
sentences.zh: 但关键是，这种情况可以激发我们中一些人的敌对想象，使我们成为邪恶的肇事者，也可以激发其他人的英雄想象。

sentences.en: It's the same situation and you're on one side or the other.
sentences.zh: 这是同样的情况，你站在一边或另一边。

sentences.en: Most people are guilty of the evil of inaction, because your mother said, "Don't get involved. Mind your own business."
sentences.zh: 大多数人都犯有不作为之罪，因为你的母亲说：“不要参与其中，管好你自己的事。”

sentences.en: And you have to say, "Mama, humanity is my business."
sentences.zh: 你必须说：“妈妈，人类是我的事。”

sentences.en: So the psychology of heroism is -- we're going to end in a moment -- how do we encourage children in new hero courses, that I'm working on with Matt Langdon -- he has a hero workshop -- to develop this heroic imagination, this self-labeling,
sentences.zh: 所以英雄主义的心理学是——我们马上就要结束——我们如何鼓励孩子们参加新的英雄课程，我正在与马特·兰登合作——他有一个英雄研讨会——来发展这种英雄想象力，这种自我标签，

sentences.en: "I am a hero in waiting," and teach them skills.
sentences.zh: “我是等待中的英雄”，并教给他们技能。

sentences.en: To be a hero, you have to learn to be a deviant, because you're always going against the conformity of the group.
sentences.zh: 要成为英雄，你必须学会​​成为一个离经叛道的人，因为你总是违背群体的一致性。

sentences.en: Heroes are ordinary people whose social actions are extraordinary. Who act.
sentences.zh: 英雄是平凡的人，但他们的社会行为却是不平凡的。谁行动。

sentences.en: The key to heroism is two things. You have to act when other people are passive.
sentences.zh: 英雄主义的关键有两点。当别人消极的时候，你必须采取行动。

sentences.en: B: You have to act socio-centrically, not egocentrically.
sentences.zh: B：你必须以社会为中心，而不是以自我为中心。

sentences.en: And I want to end with a known story about Wesley Autrey, New York subway hero.
sentences.zh: 我想以一个关于纽约地铁英雄韦斯利·奥特里 (Wesley Autrey) 的著名故事作为结尾。

sentences.en: Fifty-year-old African-American construction worker standing on a subway.
sentences.zh: 五十岁的非裔美国建筑工人站在地铁上。

sentences.en: A white guy falls on the tracks. The subway train is coming. There's 75 people there.
sentences.zh: 一个白人摔倒在铁轨上。地铁列车来了。那里有 75 个人。

sentences.en: You know what? They freeze. He's got a reason not to get involved.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？他们冻结了。他有理由不参与其中。

sentences.en: He's black, the guy's white, and he's got two kids.
sentences.zh: 他是黑人，那个人是白人，他有两个孩子。

sentences.en: Instead, he gives his kids to a stranger, jumps on the tracks, puts the guy between the tracks, lays on him, the subway goes over him.
sentences.zh: 相反，他把孩子交给了一个陌生人，跳上铁轨，把那家伙放在铁轨之间，压在他身上，地铁从他身上碾过。

sentences.en: Wesley and the guy -- 20 and a half inches height.
sentences.zh: 韦斯利和那个家伙——20英寸半高。

sentences.en: The train clearance is 21 inches. A half an inch would have taken his head off.
sentences.zh: 火车间隙为 21 英寸。半英寸就会把他的头砍掉。

sentences.en: And he said, "I did what anyone could do," no big deal to jump on the tracks.
sentences.zh: 他说，“我做了任何人都能做的事”，跳上铁轨没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: And the moral imperative is "I did what everyone should do."
sentences.zh: 道德要求是“我做了每个人都应该做的事”。

sentences.en: And so one day, you will be in a new situation.
sentences.zh: 所以有一天，你将处于一种新的境地。

sentences.en: Take path one, you're going to be a perpetrator of evil.
sentences.zh: 走第一条路，你就会成为邪恶的肇事者。

sentences.en: Evil, meaning you're going to be Arthur Andersen.
sentences.zh: 邪恶，意味着你将成为亚瑟·安德森。

sentences.en: You're going to cheat, or you're going to allow bullying.
sentences.zh: 你要么作弊，要么纵容欺凌行为。

sentences.en: Path two, you become guilty of the evil of passive inaction.
sentences.zh: 第二条路，你会因消极不作为而犯下罪恶。

sentences.en: Path three, you become a hero. The point is, are we ready to take the path to celebrating ordinary heroes, waiting for the right situation to come along to put heroic imagination into action?
sentences.zh: 第三条路，你成为英雄。关键是，我们是否准备好走上歌颂平凡英雄的道路，等待合适的时机将英雄的想象付诸行动？

sentences.en: Because it may only happen once in your life, and when you pass it by, you'll always know, I could have been a hero and I let it pass me by.
sentences.zh: 因为它可能在你的一生中只发生一次，当你错过它时，你永远会知道，我本来可以成为英雄，但我让它从我身边溜走了。

sentences.en: So the point is thinking it and then doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以重点是思考然后去做。

sentences.en: So I want to thank you. Thank you. Let's oppose the power of evil systems at home and abroad, and let's focus on the positive.
sentences.zh: 所以我想谢谢你。谢谢。让我们反对国内外邪恶制度的力量，让我们关注积极的一面。

sentences.en: Advocate for respect of personal dignity, for justice and peace, which sadly our administration has not been doing.
sentences.zh: 倡导尊重个人尊严、正义与和平，遗憾的是我们的政府并没有这样做。

sentences.en: Thanks so much. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。 （掌声）
